meta.actor: Claude — consolidation pass (no research, no content rewriting)
meta.scope: Every Grok batch file for Yemen merged into one file. Records are byte-faithful to the batches except for the normalisations listed in _consolidation.

reports.title: Central Statistical Office (Yemen) institutional core
reports.publisher: Central Statistical Office
reports.description: Primary national statistical office. Conflict has severely limited compilation capacity; extensive external capacity support is required for national accounts and external statistics. Data continuity and coverage are highly constrained.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node under severe capacity constraints.

reports.title: Population estimates
reports.publisher: CSO / UN-aligned
reports.description: Population estimates. Population is approximately 43 million; the age structure is very young and conflict-related displacement is large-scale.
reports._notes: Core demographic node. Population ~43 million.

reports.title: National Accounts of Yemen (GDP)
reports.publisher: CSO / IMF-aligned estimates
reports.description: National accounts and GDP estimates. The economy has contracted sharply under prolonged conflict; oil production is a fraction of pre-war levels and non-oil activity is severely disrupted.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node under severe conflict constraints.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.publisher: CSO / Central Bank related
reports.description: CPI and inflation rates. Inflation has been elevated and highly volatile under exchange-rate collapse, supply disruptions and dual-currency conditions.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency price node under elevated-inflation and dual-rate conditions.

reports.title: Central Bank of Yemen institutional and reporting core
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Yemen
reports.description: Central bank responsible for monetary policy, foreign-exchange management and key macro-financial statistics where published. Dual institutional realities and limited reserves constrain operations.
reports._notes: Central-bank institutional counterpart under dual and constrained conditions.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and external accounts
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Yemen / IMF-aligned
reports.description: BOP and external-sector statistics. Oil exports have collapsed; remittances, humanitarian inflows and limited formal trade dominate; reserves are critically low.
reports._notes: External-accounts node under severe constraint and large informal/humanitarian flows.

reports.title: Yemen foundational statistical-system meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from CSO and CBY sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding the CSO institutional core, population, national accounts, CPI, CBY institutional role and BOP into the opening foundation layer for Yemeni research.
reports._notes: Opening integrating node. Extreme conflict, dual institutions and data gaps should be carried forward in all subsequent batches.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch

reports.title: Oil production and export statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Oil and IMF-aligned sources
reports.description: Statistics on crude oil production and exports. Production has collapsed from pre-war peaks near 400+ thousand barrels per day to the low tens of thousands (or lower) in recent years; export interruption has been a central fiscal and external shock.
reports._notes: Core (collapsed) extractive node. Highest pre-war centrality; now a defining absence.

reports.title: Humanitarian needs and food insecurity statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from OCHA / joint monitoring and IPC-aligned sources
reports.description: Statistics on food insecurity and humanitarian needs. Inadequate food consumption affects a majority of the population in recent monitoring; severe deprivation and reliance on crisis coping strategies are widespread across both control areas.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality social and humanitarian node under current conditions.

reports.title: Dual exchange-rate and rial statistics
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Yemen / market monitoring
reports.description: Statistics and framing of the dual exchange-rate regime. Government-controlled and Ansar Allah-controlled areas maintain sharply divergent rial rates; the divergence is a structural feature of the fragmented monetary system and a key driver of inflation differentials.
reports._notes: Critical price and institutional-fragmentation node. Dual rates are a defining structural feature.

reports.title: Yemen oil–humanitarian–exchange densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from oil, humanitarian and monetary sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding collapsed oil production, humanitarian/food insecurity statistics, and dual exchange-rate statistics into a coherent extractive–humanitarian–monetary layer under severe conflict constraints.
reports._notes: Integrating node for Batch 2 domains.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
National accounts, CPI, BOP and CBY series from Batch 1

reports.title: Remittance inflows statistics and framing
reports.publisher: Derived from Cash Consortium and related sources
reports.description: Statistics and framing of remittance inflows. Remittances have become the principal source of hard currency after the collapse of oil exports, estimated at over USD 7 billion in recent years and exceeding 30% of GDP. They are a critical household survival and external-financing mechanism.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality external-financing node under current conditions. Replaces oil as the dominant hard-currency source.

reports.title: Internal displacement statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix and OCHA sources
reports.description: Statistics on internal displacement. Yemen hosts one of the world’s largest IDP populations; new displacement continues even in periods of relative de-escalation, with Ma’rib and other governorates as major destinations.
reports._notes: High-centrality humanitarian and demographic-stress node.

reports.title: Agriculture production statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from national and USDA/FAO-aligned sources
reports.description: Statistics on crop production. Sorghum, millet, wheat and other cereals are produced at low absolute levels relative to national food needs; Yemen is heavily import-dependent for staple cereals. Agriculture remains important for rural livelihoods under severe water and conflict constraints.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node under import dependence and conflict stress.

reports.title: Yemen remittances–displacement–agriculture densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from remittance, displacement and agricultural sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding remittance inflows, internal displacement statistics, and agriculture production into a coherent external-financing, humanitarian and primary-sector layer under severe conflict constraints.
reports._notes: Integrating node for Batch 3 domains.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Humanitarian, oil, exchange-rate and BOP series from earlier batches

reports.title: Fiscal balance and revenue statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from IMF-aligned and national fiscal monitoring
reports.description: Fiscal revenue, expenditure and balance indicators. Government revenues (excluding grants) have collapsed relative to pre-war levels; deficits are financed under extreme constraint with heavy reliance on grants and limited domestic sources. Dual control further fragments fiscal capacity.
reports._notes: Core fiscal-flow node under extreme revenue collapse and dual institutions.

reports.title: Education disruption and out-of-school statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from UNICEF and education monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics and framing of education access under conflict. Millions of children remain out of school; thousands of schools are damaged or destroyed. Continuously cited in humanitarian and human-capital analysis.
reports._notes: Core education densification under conflict disruption.

reports.title: Health access and nutrition statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from UNICEF / WHO and humanitarian sources
reports.description: Statistics on health-service access and malnutrition. Large shares of the population lack access to basic healthcare; severe acute malnutrition among children remains a critical emergency indicator.
reports._notes: Core health and nutrition densification under humanitarian emergency conditions.

reports.title: Yemen fiscal–education–health densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from fiscal, education and health sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding fiscal balance/revenue statistics, education disruption, and health/nutrition statistics into a coherent fiscal and human-capital residual layer under severe conflict constraints.
reports._notes: Integrating node for Batch 4 domains.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Humanitarian, remittances, oil and CPI series from earlier batches

reports.title: Internationally Recognized Government territorial control framing
reports.publisher: Derived from monitoring and reporting sources
reports.description: Framing of territorial control by the internationally recognized government and affiliated forces. Recent shifts have expanded IRG-affiliated control over large shares of southern and eastern territory (including Hadramawt and Al Maharah in recent reporting), though population centres and economic weight remain contested.
reports._notes: Primary IRG control densification. Fluid and contested.

reports.title: Ansar Allah territorial control framing
reports.publisher: Derived from monitoring and reporting sources
reports.description: Framing of territorial control by Ansar Allah (Houthis). Control is concentrated in northern highlands and includes Sana’a and a large share of the population; a parallel administrative, fiscal and monetary system operates in these areas.
reports._notes: Primary Ansar Allah control densification. Population-weighted importance is high.

reports.title: Territorial fragmentation and dual-authority framing
reports.publisher: Derived from conflict monitoring sources
reports.description: System-level framing of Yemen’s fragmented territorial and institutional landscape: dual monetary systems, dual fiscal capacities, contested ports and oil infrastructure, and multiple armed actors. Continuously cited in every macro, humanitarian and external analysis.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality structural frame for the entire Yemen graph. Underpins dual FX, dual fiscal and humanitarian patterns.
_referenced_by: All dual-rate, fiscal and humanitarian nodes

reports.title: Yemen territorial-control densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from conflict monitoring sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding IRG control framing, Ansar Allah control framing, and territorial fragmentation/dual-authority framing into a coherent territorial-dynamics layer under severe conflict constraints.
reports._notes: Integrating node for the territorial densification pass.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Dual exchange-rate, fiscal, humanitarian and oil series from earlier batches

reports.title: Saudi Arabia economic and grant support framing
reports.publisher: Derived from Saudi Program and bilateral sources
reports.description: Framing of Saudi Arabia as the principal external economic and fiscal supporter of the internationally recognized government. Grants, central-bank deposits, salary support and development projects form a critical residual financing channel under collapsed oil revenue.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality bilateral external-financing node for the IRG side.

reports.title: Major merchandise trade partners statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from trade data compilations
reports.description: Statistics on major trade partners. China, Saudi Arabia, India, Turkey and Brazil are leading import origins (food, fuel, consumer and intermediate goods); India and Saudi Arabia feature among top export destinations for residual non-oil goods. The trade deficit is large and structural.
reports._notes: Core formal trade-partner densification under constrained volumes.

reports.title: Yemen external economic and humanitarian architecture framing
reports.publisher: Derived from UN, bilateral and monitoring sources
reports.description: System-level framing of Yemen’s external architecture: Saudi and other bilateral grants, UN humanitarian system, limited formal trade, and residual diplomatic/economic engagement under conflict and dual authority. Continuously cited in every macro and humanitarian assessment.
reports._notes: Overall external-architecture densification.

reports.title: Yemen international densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from bilateral and trade sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding Saudi economic/grant support, major trade partners, and external economic/humanitarian architecture into a coherent international layer under severe conflict constraints.
reports._notes: Integrating node for the international densification pass.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Remittances, fiscal, dual FX and humanitarian series from earlier batches

_consolidation.json_syntax_repair_note: These batch files were not valid JSON as delivered: "releases_per_year" carried an unquoted text value (missing opening quote), e.g. `"releases_per_year": continuous",`. Repaired mechanically by re-quoting the value verbatim. No number was invented.
_consolidation.cadence_note: A non-numeric cadence text was moved off releases_per_year into _cadence_original verbatim and the numeric field omitted, per the v2 spec (omitted, never null). Needs a human/judgement pass to become a real number.

_normalisation.note: Second pass, 2026-08-18: mechanical alignment to src/lib/types.ts. Nothing researched, nothing invented. Every original value that was replaced is preserved on the record under a key prefixed with an underscore.
rules: jurisdiction_level mapped into the six-value union; the delivered string kept as _jurisdiction_level_original.
domains: format-normalised, then any tag outside the 22 approved values prefixed "proposed:" as the spec directs. No semantic merging was done — that needs your call.

relationship_type: part_of edges moved onto the child node as part_of; contains edges reversed onto the child; produced_by edges dropped (publisher is a string, not a node); related_to / complements held in _dropped as deferred. Off-union values were poisoning every PageRank score with NaN.
last_updated added as null where absent (required field, string|null).
region filled with the country name where it was null or missing.
releases_per_year: unambiguous single-word cadences resolved to numbers; ambiguous text left in _cadence_original and listed under _gaps.unresolved_cadence.
source_kind mapped to official/commercial; delivered value kept as _source_kind_original.
Non-schema keys Grok wrote (shape, notes, referenced_by, ...) renamed with a leading underscore so they are visibly not part of the schema. Nothing deleted.

_gaps.note: What is genuinely missing and cannot be fixed mechanically — this is the research queue, not a defect list.
